title: Semantic Tokens
summary: Explain the Semantic Tokens workflow, ownership boundaries, registry, target lookup, and generated usage index.
content_html:
Semantic Tokens

Semantic Tokens let an author associate displayed Markdown text with a stable target identity. They are a manage-mode Docs Viewer capability; Catalogue is the registered family, with Work, Series, and Moment targets.

Workflow

  1. In Markdown source, choose Add catalogue token.
  2. Search the combined Catalogue list, select the exact target, confirm the occurrence Title, and add the token.
  3. Put the caret in an existing token to inspect it. Its Title can be updated or the token removed; its target identity is read-only, so retargeting is Remove followed by Add.
  4. Rebuild resolves a recognized token only when the target lookup supplies a workable destination. Unresolved token-like text remains ordinary text and does not block the build.
  5. The manage-only Semantic Tokens Report lists resolved occurrences for a selected scope and links to their documents. Docs Broken Links diagnoses unresolved occurrences and hands repair back to the source editor.

Ownership

  • Docs Viewer source-editor core owns the Markdown buffer, selection, dirty state, save, and Rebuild workflow.
  • Catalogue owns its canonical Work, Series, and Moment records and the reusable mixed-target discovery list.
  • The Docs Viewer Semantic Tokens feature owns token definitions, parsing, build-time resolution, generated usage data, and the resolved-token report.
  • Docs Broken Links owns read-only failure diagnosis. The author remains in control of source or canonical-data repair.

Registry And Generated Data

The checked-in token-definition registry is:

docs-viewer/config/semantic-tokens/registry.json

The rebuildable manage target lookup is:

docs-viewer/data/generated/semantic-tokens/target-lookup.json

Each scope's resolved usage index is:

docs-viewer/scopes/<scope>/published/documents/semantic-tokens/index.json

The usage index records occurrences in documents; it is not a registry or a canonical target store. The registry, target lookup, and usage directory are manage-only and are omitted from the public publish projection.
